feed.title: Data Engineering — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Airbyte
entry.summary: Open-source data integration (ELT) with a huge connector catalogue; self-hostable.

entry.title: Apache Flink
entry.summary: A real-time stream-processing engine that handles events as they arrive, with low latency. Unlike Spark’s batch roots it treats streaming as the first-class model.

entry.title: Apache Iceberg
entry.summary: An open table format for large analytical tables, giving schema evolution, time travel and atomic writes. Unlike a raw Parquet directory it manages the table as a consistent, versioned unit.

entry.title: Apache Spark
entry.summary: An engine that processes big data in a distributed, in-memory way — batch and streaming. Unlike single-machine libraries it splits terabytes across a cluster and processes them in parallel.

entry.title: Awesome Data Engineering
entry.summary: A list gathering every layer of data engineering — ingestion, storage, processing, orchestration — with tools. Unlike single-tool lists it maps the whole stack.

entry.title: Awesome Hadoop
entry.summary: A resource list for Hadoop, the distributed storage and processing framework.

entry.title: Awesome HPC
entry.summary: A list of tools, libraries and resources for high-performance computing (HPC).

entry.title: Awesome Spark
entry.summary: A list of packages, tutorials and examples for the Apache Spark ecosystem. Unlike the official docs it gathers community libraries and real-world examples.

entry.title: ClickHouse
entry.summary: A columnar OLAP database for analytics, extremely fast at aggregations at scale.

entry.title: Dagster
entry.summary: An orchestrator centred on data assets, tracking each table as an “asset”. Unlike Airflow it focuses on the data produced rather than the task, with data quality built in.

entry.title: Data Engineering Podcast
entry.summary: Long-form interviews digging deep into data-engineering tools and architectures.

entry.title: DataTalks.Club
entry.summary: A free community offering hands-on data-engineering and ML zoomcamps.

entry.title: dbt
entry.summary: A tool managing data-warehouse transformations with SQL + version control + tests. Unlike hand-written SQL scripts it brings a dependency graph, docs and tests like a software project.

entry.title: Delta Lake
entry.summary: An open storage layer bringing ACID transactions and time travel to data lakes.

entry.title: DuckDB
entry.summary: An in-process analytical database — no server, it queries files directly. Unlike server-based warehouses it is “OLAP at SQLite speed” on one machine, over Parquet/CSV.

entry.title: Great Expectations
entry.summary: A data-quality framework that validates and documents data with declarative expectations.

entry.title: Hamilton
entry.summary: A lightweight Python library that builds data transformations as a graph from functions. Unlike heavy orchestrators it gives a dependency graph in a single file with no infrastructure.

entry.title: Meltano
entry.summary: An open-source DataOps ELT platform, Singer-based and CLI/config-driven.

entry.title: Spark Internals
entry.summary: A deep document on how Apache Spark works inside — scheduling, shuffle, memory. Unlike a usage guide it opens up the engine, for performance tuning.

entry.title: Trino
entry.summary: A distributed SQL query engine that queries data where it lives, across many sources.

entry.title: Data Engineering Zoomcamp
entry.summary: A free, project-based course teaching data engineering end to end (Docker, dbt, Spark, Kafka, cloud). Unlike scattered tutorials it has you build a real pipeline from start to finish.

entry.title: Microsoft · Data Engineer Path
entry.summary: A Microsoft learning path teaching cloud data engineering module by module. Unlike product docs it is framed as an ordered, exam-measured skill path.

entry.title: Databricks
entry.summary: A cloud platform built on Spark that merges the data lake and warehouse (“lakehouse”). Unlike running a separate warehouse and lake it unites them under one governance and notebook interface.

entry.title: Apache Kafka
entry.summary: Retains messages after consumption, with consumers carrying their own offsets so they can replay history. That durability is the real split from classic queues.
